hospitals.description: K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital is the pediatric arm of Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune, a few minutes inland from Asbury Park and Ocean Grove. It is the main tertiary pediatric referral point for Monmouth and Ocean counties, with a 24 hour pediatric emergency department, a 10 room PICU, a Level III NICU and general pediatric inpatient units. In 2025 the American College of Surgeons verified the campus as a Level I pediatric trauma center, the first in New Jersey, which makes it the shore's destination for seriously injured children. The children's hospital shares the large JSUMC campus on Route 33, which also houses the 2019 HOPE Tower and a busy adult Level I trauma program. For someone living in Asbury Park this is the closest and most acute pediatric employer in the region.
highlights: Closest major pediatric hospital to Asbury Park, roughly 3 miles
ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center since March 2025, first in NJ
10 room PICU and Level III NICU; AACN Beacon Award (gold) for NICU and PICU
Ranked #1 children's hospital in NJ by U.S. News (tied with Joseph M. Sanzari Children's)
Pediatric ED open 24/7 since 2017, about 20,000 pediatric ED visits a year
State designated children's hospital since 2006; Regional Perinatal Center on site

hospitals.notes: Parent Jersey Shore University Medical Center (691 beds per Wikipedia) is not listed separately; pediatric postings name JSUMC or K. Hovnanian and show location US-NJ-Neptune. Bed figures vary by source: Wikipedia lists 88 total pediatric beds and a 30 bed NICU, the HMH site lists 30 inpatient beds plus the 10 room PICU, and a 2017 HMH notice cited a 34 bed NICU. Wikipedia says ANCC Magnet in 2012 and 2017; current Magnet status not confirmed. Pediatric hospitalist and PICU teams also cover sister sites Ocean University (Brick) and Riverview (Red Bank).

hospitals.description: Unterberg Children's Hospital is the pediatric service of Monmouth Medical Center, a 514 bed RWJBarnabas teaching hospital on a 21 acre campus in Long Branch, about 6 miles north of Asbury Park along the coast. It was licensed by New Jersey as a children's hospital for Monmouth and Ocean counties in 2006 and runs a pediatric residency, a dedicated pediatric emergency department, a small PICU and a large state designated Level III NICU. The NICU was the first Level III unit in New Jersey and admits roughly 500 to 550 infants a year, fed by an obstetric service that delivers more than 6,500 babies annually. In January 2026 the state approved RWJBarnabas plans to move maternity, pediatric and inpatient medical surgical care to a new hospital on the Vogel Medical Campus in Tinton Falls, targeted for about 2032.
highlights: About 6 miles from Asbury Park
First Level III NICU in New Jersey; region's largest state designated Level III NICU
More than 6,500 births a year at the Eisenberg Family Center
Magnet hospital with Magnet with Distinction honors
Pediatric residency program and Rutgers RWJMS regional campus
Pediatric and maternity services planned to relocate to Tinton Falls around 2032

hospitals.description: Riverview Medical Center is a Hackensack Meridian Health hospital on the Navesink River in downtown Red Bank, about 10 miles north of Asbury Park. It began in 1922 as a small sanitarium and grew into a roughly 450 to 476 bed regional hospital that merged into Meridian Health in 1997. It runs a labor and delivery service designated as an Intermediate Community Perinatal Center, but it reported no special care nursery or NICU, and sicker newborns and children are referred to K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital in Neptune. A $55 million emergency care center is in planning and will include pediatric friendly treatment beds. For a pediatric NP, this is mainly a source of ED, newborn or float roles rather than a peds unit.
highlights: About 10 miles north of Asbury Park in walkable Red Bank
Intermediate Community Perinatal Center (labor and delivery, no NICU reported)
ANCC Magnet in 2012 and 2017 per Wikipedia
Planned $55 million Alton A. Hovnanian Emergency Care Center with pediatric friendly beds
Part of the Hackensack Meridian Health Jersey Shore network with K. Hovnanian Children's as pediatric hub
hospitals.notes: Included because Jersey Shore is a hotspot. No inpatient pediatric unit was confirmed this session (absence not proven). Magnet status after 2017 not confirmed. Pediatric hospitalist or newborn roles, if any, would post under Hackensack Meridian with location Red Bank.

hospitals.description: Ocean University Medical Center is a 318 bed Hackensack Meridian teaching hospital in Brick Township, about 15 miles south of Asbury Park off the Garden State Parkway. It traces back to a four room hospital in Point Pleasant Beach in 1918, opened on the Brick campus in 1984, and took its current name in 2021 to reflect its residency programs. Its emergency department, expanded in 2014, includes a dedicated pediatric emergency area staffed in peak hours by pediatric emergency physicians linked to K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital. The maternity service has a Level II NICU (special care nursery) with neonatologists on site around the clock, and higher acuity babies and children go to Neptune.
highlights: About 15 miles south of Asbury Park
Dedicated pediatric emergency area within the ED, affiliated with K. Hovnanian Children's
Level II NICU / special care nursery with 24/7 neonatologists
ANCC Magnet recognized
Teaching hospital with about 90 residents (2021)
hospitals.notes: Pediatric emergency center hours were part-day when reported in 2011 (weekday afternoons and evenings, weekend 1 to 11 p.m.); current hours not confirmed. Wikipedia says pediatric patients are cared for by K. Hovnanian physicians, but a staffed inpatient pediatric unit was not confirmed, so peds_inpatient is false pending verification.

hospitals.description: Community Medical Center is RWJBarnabas Health's 592 bed hospital in Toms River, the largest hospital in Ocean County and about 25 miles south of Asbury Park. It opened in 1961 as a 50 bed community hospital, built one of the largest emergency departments on the East Coast in the 2000s, and became a teaching hospital in 2021 when its first Rutgers residents arrived. A $600 million, decade long campus expansion began in late 2021. Its maternity service is designated an Intermediate Community Perinatal Center with an on site special care or intermediate nursery. Dedicated pediatric inpatient and pediatric ED services were not confirmed in this session.
highlights: Largest hospital in Ocean County at 592 beds
About 25 miles south of Asbury Park
Intermediate Community Perinatal Center with special care nursery
Teaching hospital since 2021 through a Rutgers partnership
$600 million campus expansion under way since 2021
Level 3 epilepsy center (NAEC)
hospitals.notes: Included because Jersey Shore is a hotspot. NICU level 2 is inferred from its NJ Intermediate Community Perinatal Center designation with a nursery reported on site (ACNJ 2025 data); unit size not found. Pediatric unit status unverified this session; the RWJBH hospital page could not be fetched. Toms River is a large retiree market, so adult and ED roles dominate.
